title: Deuteronomy Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 3.

questions.question: Who came out against the Israelites to battle at Edrei?
questions.correctAnswer: Og king of Bashan
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:1 states that Og the king of Bashan came out against them to battle at Edrei.

questions.question: What did the LORD say to Moses regarding Og king of Bashan?
options: Fear him not, for I will deliver him into your hand
Engage him in peace talks first
Build a wall to protect from him
Ignore him and continue your journey
questions.correctAnswer: Fear him not, for I will deliver him into your hand
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:2 records the LORD telling Moses not to fear Og because He will deliver him and his land into Moses' hand.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the battle with Og king of Bashan?
options: Og and all his people were smitten until none remained
questions.correctAnswer: Og and all his people were smitten until none remained
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:3 explains that the LORD delivered Og into their hands and they smote him until none was left.

questions.question: How many cities did the Israelites take from the kingdom of Og in Bashan?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:4 states they took threescore (60) cities in all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og.

questions.question: How were the cities of Og described in terms of fortifications?
options: Fenced with high walls, gates, and bars
questions.correctAnswer: Fenced with high walls, gates, and bars
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:5 describes all the cities as fenced with high walls, gates, and bars.

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites spared the men, women, and children of every city in Bashan.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:6 says they utterly destroyed the men, women, and children of every city, as they had done to Sihon.

questions.question: What did the Israelites do with the cattle and spoil of the cities they captured?
options: They took them as prey for themselves
They gave them to the Levites
They left them for the Amorites
questions.correctAnswer: They took them as prey for themselves
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:7 states that all the cattle and spoil of the cities were taken as prey by the Israelites.

questions.question: From where to where did the Israelites take the land from the two kings of the Amorites?
options: From the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon
From the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea
From the Jordan River to the Dead Sea
questions.correctAnswer: From the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:8 specifies the land taken was from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon.

questions.question: True or False: Mount Hermon was called Sirion by the Sidonians and Shenir by the Amorites.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:9 explains the different names for mount Hermon by Sidonians and Amorites.

questions.question: What areas did the Israelites possess including the cities of the kingdom of Og?
options: All the cities of the plain, all Gilead, and all Bashan unto Salchah and Edrei
The land west of Jordan only
questions.correctAnswer: All the cities of the plain, all Gilead, and all Bashan unto Salchah and Edrei
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:10 states that they possessed all the cities of the plain, Gilead, and Bashan unto Salchah and Edrei.

questions.question: What was unique about Og king of Bashan's bedstead?
options: It was made of iron and very large
It was made of gold and jewels
questions.correctAnswer: It was made of iron and very large
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:11 describes Og’s bedstead as made of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits wide.

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites took possession of half the valley from Gilead to the river Jabbok and beyond.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:16 states the Reubenites and Gadites received from Gilead to the river Arnon and the border to the river Jabbok, not beyond.

questions.question: Who was given the land of Bashan and the rest of Gilead?
questions.correctAnswer: The half tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:13 says the rest of Gilead and all Bashan were given to the half tribe of Manasseh.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 3, which instruction comes first?
options: Do not fear the kings; the LORD will fight for you
Pass over armed before your brethren
Besought the LORD to let Moses cross Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: Pass over armed before your brethren
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:18 commands the people to pass over armed before their brethren before other instructions appear.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was allowed by the LORD to cross over the Jordan to see the good land.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:26-27 records the LORD’s anger and refusal to let Moses cross the Jordan.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was unique about Og king of Bashan according to Deuteronomy 3?
options: He was the only king left from the giants
He was the tallest man in Israel
He ruled over all the Amorites
He had a large army of chariots
questions.correctAnswer: He was the only king left from the giants
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:11 states that Og king of Bashan was the only remaining king from the remnant of giants, highlighting his uniqueness among defeated rulers.

questions.question: To whom was the land from Aroer by the river Arnon and half of mount Gilead given?
questions.correctAnswer: The Reubenites and the Gadites
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:12 clearly assigns this territory to the Reubenites and the Gadites, showing the division of the conquered lands among the tribes.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 3 teach about trust in God's provision through the example of the land distribution?
options: By showing God gave the land to each tribe as a promise to be trusted
By instructing the tribes to fight for the land by their own strength
By encouraging tribes to negotiate the land among themselves
By warning the tribes to avoid the land for fear of enemies
questions.correctAnswer: By showing God gave the land to each tribe as a promise to be trusted
questions.explanation: Verses 12–13 demonstrate that God allotted the land to the tribes, teaching believers to trust in God's promises and provision rather than their own efforts.

questions.question: Who took all the country of Argob and named it Bashanhavothjair?
questions.correctAnswer: Jair the son of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:14 tells that Jair, son of Manasseh, took the country of Argob and named it after himself, illustrating personal leadership and legacy.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 3, what was given to Machir?
options: The land of the children of Ammon
questions.correctAnswer: Gilead
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:15 explicitly states that Gilead was given to Machir, showing the continued allotment of the land among the tribes.

questions.question: True or False: The Reubenites and Gadites were given land that extended from Gilead even unto the river Arnon and the river Jabbok.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:16 confirms that the Reubenites and Gadites received land from Gilead to the river Arnon and Jabbok, indicating the extent of their inheritance.

questions.question: Which geographical areas are mentioned as part of the land given in Deuteronomy 3:17?
options: The plain, Jordan, and the coast from Chinnereth to the salt sea
Mount Sinai and the wilderness of Paran
The land of Canaan and Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The plain, Jordan, and the coast from Chinnereth to the salt sea
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:17 describes the land including the plain, Jordan, and the coast from Chinnereth to the salt sea, showing the broad territory given to the tribes.

questions.question: What instruction did Moses give concerning the men who were fit for war as stated in Deuteronomy 3?
options: They should pass over armed before their brethren
They should stay behind and guard the cities
They should be exempt from battle
They should divide into small groups and scout
questions.correctAnswer: They should pass over armed before their brethren
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:18 commands that all who are fit for war should pass over armed before their brethren, showing the importance of readiness and protection for the community.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 3:19, where were the wives, little ones, and cattle to remain during the war?
options: In the cities given to them
In the land of the children of Ammon
questions.correctAnswer: In the cities given to them
questions.explanation: Verse 19 instructs that the families and cattle should stay in the cities assigned to them, emphasizing protection and provision during conflict.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 3:20 say will happen once the LORD has given rest to the brethren and they possess the land beyond Jordan?
options: Each man will return to his possession
They will build altars to the LORD
They will make a covenant of peace
They will send offerings to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Each man will return to his possession
questions.explanation: Verse 20 promises that after rest and possession of the land, each man shall return to the possession given to him, emphasizing order and inheritance.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 3:21 teach about the role of Joshua and the works of the LORD?
options: Joshua has witnessed the LORD’s victories over the two kings and will lead Israel to inherit the land
Joshua must conquer the land alone without God's help
Joshua is to wait for Moses to lead the battles
Joshua will divide the spoils of war among the tribes
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua has witnessed the LORD’s victories over the two kings and will lead Israel to inherit the land
questions.explanation: Verse 21 shows Joshua's firsthand experience of God's power and his leadership role in guiding Israel to inherit the promised land.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 3:22 assures the people that they should fear their enemies because they must fight alone.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states the opposite: the people should not fear their enemies because the LORD will fight for them, emphasizing trust in God's protection.

questions.question: What virtue is demonstrated by Moses when he prays to the LORD in Deuteronomy 3:23-24?
options: Humility and reverence for God's mighty works
Anger and impatience with God's timing
questions.correctAnswer: Humility and reverence for God's mighty works
questions.explanation: Moses expresses awe and acknowledges God's greatness, demonstrating humility and reverence as he prays (verses 23-24).

questions.question: Based on Deuteronomy 3:25-26, what lesson can be learned about submitting to God's will when desires are denied?
options: Accepting God’s will even when personal requests are refused
Continuing to argue with God until He agrees
Ignoring God’s commands and acting independently
Seeking assistance from others to change God’s mind
questions.correctAnswer: Accepting God’s will even when personal requests are refused
questions.explanation: Moses asks to cross over but God refuses and commands him to accept this limitation, teaching submission to God's sovereign will.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 3:27-28 instructs Moses to encourage Joshua because Joshua will lead the people to inherit the land Moses will see but not enter.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verses command Moses to encourage Joshua who will lead the people across the Jordan to inherit the land Moses can only view, highlighting leadership transition and encouragement.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 3.

questions.question: What was the command given to Joshua regarding the people, as stated in Deuteronomy 3:28?
options: To lead the people into battle and cause them to inherit the land
To build altars and offer sacrifices
To write down the laws given by Moses
To divide the land among the tribes
questions.correctAnswer: To lead the people into battle and cause them to inherit the land
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:28 commands Joshua to be encouraged and strengthened because he will lead the people across the Jordan and cause them to inherit the land.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 3:22, why were the Israelites instructed not to fear their enemies?
options: Because the LORD their God would fight for them
Because the enemy was too few in number
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD their God would fight for them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:22 clearly states that the Israelites should not fear their enemies because the LORD their God will fight for them.

questions.question: What was the request Moses made to the LORD in Deuteronomy 3:25?
options: To allow him to cross over and see the good land beyond Jordan
To give him victory over all enemies
To grant him long life to lead Israel
To provide water in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: To allow him to cross over and see the good land beyond Jordan
questions.explanation: In Deuteronomy 3:25, Moses prays to see the good land beyond Jordan, including the goodly mountain and Lebanon.

questions.question: How did the LORD respond to Moses’ request to cross over into the promised land, according to Deuteronomy 3:26?
options: He was angry and refused to let Moses cross
He granted Moses permission to cross
He told Moses to build an altar first
He asked Moses to appoint Joshua as leader
questions.correctAnswer: He was angry and refused to let Moses cross
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:26 states that the LORD was wroth with Moses for the people's sake and would not hear his request to cross over.

questions.question: What did Moses see from the top of Pisgah as commanded in Deuteronomy 3:27?
options: The land westward, northward, southward, and eastward
questions.correctAnswer: The land westward, northward, southward, and eastward
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:27 directs Moses to look in all directions from Pisgah to behold the land he would not enter.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 3:29, where did the Israelites settle after these events?
options: In the valley over against Bethpeor
At the foot of Mount Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: In the valley over against Bethpeor
questions.explanation: Verse 29 states that the Israelites abode in the valley opposite Bethpeor after these events.

questions.question: The statement 'Ye shall not fear them: for the LORD your God he shall fight for you' in Deuteronomy 3:22 is an example of which literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Assurance through divine promise
questions.explanation: This verse uses a direct assurance, a promise from God, to encourage Israel not to fear, which is a literary device of divine reassurance.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God fighting for His people as seen in Deuteronomy 3:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 14:14
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:14 states, 'The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace,' echoing the promise in Deuteronomy 3:22 about God fighting for His people.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 3:24, Moses praises the LORD's greatness and mighty hand. What theological theme does this reflect that is developed throughout the Pentateuch?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty and unmatched power
questions.explanation: The verse reflects the theme of God’s unmatched power and sovereignty, a central theme throughout the Pentateuch highlighting God’s ability to act mightily for His people.

questions.question: Which tribe was given the land of Gilead according to Deuteronomy 3:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Machir
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:15 explicitly states that Gilead was given to Machir.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'fear' in Deuteronomy 3:22 primarily means what?
questions.correctAnswer: To be afraid or terrified
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'yare' (ירא) used here means 'to fear' in the sense of being afraid or terrified, which God commands the Israelites not to experience because He will fight for them.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 3:21, what is the significance of Joshua's eyes having seen what the LORD did to the two kings?
options: It serves as a demonstration of God's power to be repeated in future conquests
It means Joshua witnessed the building of the tabernacle
It indicates Joshua saw the wilderness wanderings
It refers to Joshua's seeing the promised land from Pisgah
questions.correctAnswer: It serves as a demonstration of God's power to be repeated in future conquests
questions.explanation: The verse shows that the defeat of the two kings is a pattern for God's power that Joshua will experience as he leads Israel into future battles.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 3:20, the tribes given land on this side of Jordan were to immediately return to their possessions after the initial conquest.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:20 states they were to remain in their cities until the LORD gave rest to their brethren and they possessed the land beyond Jordan; only then would they return.

questions.question: True or False: The bedstead of Og king of Bashan described in Deuteronomy 3:11 symbolizes the remnant of the giants among the Amorites.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:11 describes Og's iron bedstead as a symbol of his giant stature, representing the last remnant of the giants in that region.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God fighting on behalf of His people as seen in Deuteronomy 3:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:31
questions.explanation: Romans 8:31 states, 'If God be for us, who can be against us?' echoing the theme of divine protection and victory in Deuteronomy 3:22.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's assurance to not fear King Og and his people in battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:2 shows God assuring Moses not to fear Og because He will deliver him and his land into their hands, demonstrating God's omnipotence over earthly kings and armies.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 3:11, what does the size and material of Og's bedstead signify about the nature of the people he ruled over?
questions.correctAnswer: They were giants
questions.explanation: Verse 11 states Og was the remnant of giants and his iron bedstead measured nine by four cubits, indicating the extraordinary size and strength of his people.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted by the complete destruction of the men, women, and children of Bashan as described in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine Judgment
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:6 records the utter destruction of Bashan’s inhabitants, illustrating the doctrine of divine judgment against sin and disobedience.

questions.question: How does the chapter describe the distribution of the conquered land among the tribes of Israel?
options: Divided between the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh
All given to the tribe of Judah
Held in common by all tribes
questions.correctAnswer: Divided between the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 3:12-13 explains the land possession was given to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh after conquest.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Deuteronomy 3:22 and 3:2 convey about God's relationship with His people in conflict?
options: God fights for His people and they should not fear their enemies
God punishes those who go to war
questions.correctAnswer: God fights for His people and they should not fear their enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 3:2 and 3:22 reveal that God promises to deliver and fight for His people, instructing them not to fear their enemies, showing divine protection and sovereignty.

questions.question: What does Moses’ request to see the good land beyond Jordan (Deuteronomy 3:25) reveal about human desire and divine sovereignty?
options: Desire for earthly reward without obedience
Human longing for promised blessing constrained by God's will
questions.correctAnswer: Human longing for promised blessing constrained by God's will
questions.explanation: Moses’ petition in 3:25 expresses his deep desire to see the promised land, but God's refusal (3:26-27) demonstrates divine sovereignty over human aspiration.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is gained by combining the account of God giving rest to the people (3:20) and His command to pass over armed before brethren (3:18)?
options: God’s providential guidance and sanctification through warfare
The necessity of peace without preparation
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providential guidance and sanctification through warfare
questions.explanation: Verses 3:18 and 3:20 together show that God provides rest and land possession through divine guidance and the sanctifying process of armed conflict in His plan.

questions.question: In the broader redemptive narrative, how does the charge given to Joshua in Deuteronomy 3:28 reflect God's covenant faithfulness?
options: It shows God abandoning His promises
It demonstrates God’s ongoing commitment to fulfill the land promise through Joshua
It reveals a new covenant unrelated to the past
It limits God's power to Moses only
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God’s ongoing commitment to fulfill the land promise through Joshua
questions.explanation: Verse 3:28 shows Moses commanded to encourage Joshua, who will lead the people to inherit the land, reflecting God's faithfulness to His covenant promise.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly seen in Moses’ praise of God's mighty hand in Deuteronomy 3:24?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s omnipotence
questions.explanation: Moses’ praise in 3:24 highlights God’s mighty hand and great works unmatched in heaven or earth, indicating His omnipotence.

questions.question: How does the conquest of the land from the two Amorite kings (verse 8) typologically reflect Christ’s ultimate victory over evil?
options: It does not relate to Christ
It foreshadows Christ’s defeat of Satan and sin by divine authority
It symbolizes Christ’s earthly ministry only
It represents human military success alone
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ’s defeat of Satan and sin by divine authority
questions.explanation: The conquest over Amorite kings in 3:8 typifies Christ’s ultimate triumph over evil forces, showing God’s authority over spiritual and earthly powers.

questions.question: What apologetic answer does Deuteronomy 3:23-26 provide to sceptics who claim God is unjust for not allowing Moses to enter the Promised Land?
options: God’s holiness and sovereignty require obedience and timing in His plans
God is indifferent to human leadership
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and sovereignty require obedience and timing in His plans
questions.explanation: Verses 3:23-26 reveal Moses’ plea and God’s refusal, emphasizing God’s sovereign justice and timing, not arbitrariness, countering claims of injustice.

questions.question: What does the narrative arc of conquering Bashan and distributing its land (verses 4-14) teach about God’s promise and fulfillment to Israel?
options: God’s promises are conditional and often fail
God fulfills His covenant promises by enabling Israel to possess the land
God’s promises are only spiritual, not territorial
questions.correctAnswer: God fulfills His covenant promises by enabling Israel to possess the land
questions.explanation: Verses 3:4-14 describe the military victory and land division, illustrating God's faithfulness in fulfilling covenant promises to Israel.

questions.question: Which doctrine is underscored by the command to the Reubenites and Gadites to remain with their families and cattle during warfare (Deuteronomy 3:19)?
options: Doctrine of stewardship and orderly inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of stewardship and orderly inheritance
questions.explanation: Verse 3:19 commands the tribes to stay with their possessions, teaching orderly stewardship and respect for God's provision during warfare.

questions.question: How does the description of cities and fortifications in Deuteronomy 3:5 emphasize God’s power in conquest?
options: God’s power is limited by human walls
God alone can overcome fortified cities and numerous towns
questions.correctAnswer: God alone can overcome fortified cities and numerous towns
questions.explanation: Verse 3:5 highlights many fenced cities with high walls and bars, yet God enabled Israel to capture them all, demonstrating divine power over human defenses.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Deuteronomy 3:7 and 3:6 provide about God's justice and provision after judgment?
options: God punishes but also provides spoil for His people
questions.correctAnswer: God punishes but also provides spoil for His people
questions.explanation: Verses 3:6 and 3:7 show God’s judgment through destruction of people but provision through taking spoil for Israel, balancing justice and blessing.
